title: 打错了
setting: London, Sunday, 10 am. A number from China, where it's dinner time.

granny.name: 奶奶
granny.en: a grandma in Harbin, calling her grandchild

xiaobao.name: 小宝
xiaobao.en: her grandchild, in the next room

hangup.en: It's gone quiet. Grandma's hanging up, then.
She hung up. Ten minutes later she rings again, to check you've eaten.

say.en: An unknown number from China. Pick up: say hello.
say.tip: 喂 wéi = hello, but only on the phone.

1.en: An unknown number from China. Pick up: say hello, politely.
1.tip: 喂，您好 = hello, on the phone: 您 is the polite 'you', for someone you don't know.

steps.en: I've made dumplings. Come home and eat!

say.en: She thinks you're her grandchild, 小宝. You're not: tell her.
say.tip: 不是不是 = no, no: said twice, it's a quick, friendly 'you've got it wrong'.

silence.en: Nothing to say? Then hurry home!

hangup.en: She hung up happy. In Harbin, a plate of dumplings is waiting for a grandchild who isn't you.

ok.en: Stop fooling around! The dumplings are in the pot!

1.tip: 我不是… = I'm not…: 不是 before a name says who you aren't.

say.en: She thinks you're joking. Tell her it's a wrong number.
say.tip: 打错了 = wrong number (打 = dial, 错 = wrong).

1.tip: 您打错了 = you've got the wrong number, with 您, the polite 'you', for someone older.

say.en: A stranger's grandma wants to know if you've eaten. Tell her you have.

not.note: That's her question back. Answer it: 吃了！ (I have).

say.tip: 吃了吗 (have you eaten?) is how grandmas say 'I care about you'. The answer is 吃了！

fail.en: Eh? Have you eaten or not?

1.en: A stranger's grandma wants to know if you've eaten. Tell her you have, and thank her.
1.tip: 吃过了 = I've (already) eaten: 过 says it's done.

steps.en: Oh my! Xiaobao was home all along!
Well, you eat plenty too, dear!

say.en: She's found 小宝. Say goodbye to her.
say.tip: 奶奶 nǎinai = Grandma: what you call any grandmother, yours or not.

1.en: She's found 小宝. Say goodbye, and leave her to her dumplings.
1.tip: 您慢慢吃 = take your time, enjoy your meal: what you say to anyone sitting down to eat. 您 is the polite 'you'.

steps.en: Wrong number, right grandma. In Harbin, 小宝 gets the dumplings. In London, you suddenly want some.
steps.zh: 打错一个电话，多了一个奶奶。
